move: rotated halftone dot screen renders a sun and word, screen angle breathes
how: A canvas draws a low-res source each frame: a vertical white-to-grey gradient, a shaded sun disc that swings across and up on a cosine arc once per D, and the word RETRO along the bottom. The output samples that source on a rotated lattice of 14px cells and fills a dark dot per cell whose radius grows with darkness, on a cream background. The screen angle drifts 0.26 rad plus or minus 0.06 and the dot gain 1 plus or minus 0.12, each one sine cycle per D, so the print screen seems to breathe; every quantity is periodic so the loop closes.
adapt: Replace drawSource with the product image or logo (same-origin so getImageData works), change the word, the paper and ink colours, and CELL for coarser or finer dots. Keep the angle and gain breathing to avoid a static screen.
port: mount(el, shot) creates the output canvas and offscreen source canvas; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one linear progress tween over D whose onUpdate draws the source and rasterises the dots, replacing fx.register. Wait for the font before the first frame. gsap.min.js is loaded but unused in the original.
caveats: loads gsap but does not use it
per-frame getImageData plus roughly 6000 arcs; acceptable at 1280x720
the source picture is procedural, not an uploaded image
